rules: One click listener on document handles every interactive element.
el = event.target.closest('[data-act]'). If there is none, the listener returns and the click is not handled.

raw = el.dataset.act. i = raw.indexOf(':'). If i < 0: verb = raw and arg = undefined. Otherwise verb = raw.slice(0, i) and arg = raw.slice(i + 1), so only the FIRST colon splits and the arg keeps any later colons (push:note:n1 gives verb 'push', arg 'note:n1').
If el is an <a>, event.preventDefault() is called.
event.stopPropagation() is always called, whether or not a handler exists.

fn = A[verb]. If fn exists it is called as fn(arg, el): the arg is always a string or undefined (handlers convert with unary + where they need a number), and the element is the second parameter. The return value (some handlers are async) is ignored.
If A[verb] does not exist nothing else happens: no error, no toast, no fallback.
The nearest ancestor with data-act wins (closest), so a data-act inside another data-act never reaches the outer one.
There are no verb-specific branches in the dispatcher. push, tab, sheet, toast and the rest are ordinary entries of A (see coreHandlers).
A <button disabled> does not fire click in the browser, so the verb of a disabled button is never dispatched.

coreHandlers.back: function () { const t = S.stack[S.stack.length - 1]; _b4(); if (t && t.id === 'xray') { closeSheet(); const p = S.stack[S.stack.length - 1]; if (p && p.id === 'xrayhome') setTimeout(() => refreshPage(p), 60); if (S.rendered) renderLearn(); } }

coreHandlerNotes.push: closeSheet(); then the arg is split once more at its first colon when that colon is not at index 0: push(view, viewArg), else push(arg). The Notes Tracker script wraps it (the code shown): 'note:new' opens the new-note sheet through A.ntNew() and everything else goes to the original.
coreHandlerNotes.back: A.back is assigned again after every wrap of the global back() (L8374, L8550, L10060), so it is the newest wrapper: the code shown runs _b4() (the previous wrapper), which runs the one before, down to the original back() at L6488.
coreHandlerNotes.tab: closeSheet(); setTab(arg); and the tab's scroll position is reset to the top.
coreHandlerNotes.sheet: openSheet(SHEETS[arg](), tall) where tall is true only for 'allTools'.
coreHandlerNotes.toast: toast(arg, 'check'): the arg text is shown with the check icon for 2400 ms.
coreHandlerNotes.tool: A.tool is the ORIGINAL openTool (L6954-L6960), captured when A was created. Later scripts reassign the global openTool twice (L8228, L8369) to redirect xray, notes, tests, mindmap, cloud and querydb, but A.tool is never reassigned and nothing else calls openTool(), so those redirects do not apply to data-act="tool:…" clicks. See handlerNote on the verb.
coreHandlerNotes.jump: Only used by the desktop jump panel and the location.hash start (line 8682-8683): jumps straight to a stage, tab or a few named screens.

dispatcher.keyboard: A separate keydown listener on document (L7070-L7073): Escape closes the open sheet, else pops the top page when S.stack is not empty; '/' opens the search sheet (cmdk) when S.stage === 'app' and focus is not in an input or textarea.

dynamicSites.expression: c.id ? (c.id === 'c1' ? 'push:lesson' : 'push:course:' + c.id) : 'toast:Course preview would open here'
